sources.title: Discovery of a big void in Khufu’s Pyramid by observation of cosmic-ray muons
sources.notes: Human-approved. Supports a large void above the Grand Gallery with minimum length 30 m, detected using three muon technologies and independent analyses. Its intended purpose is unknown; call it a void, not a chamber, room, tomb, or treasure space.

sources.title: Precise characterization of a corridor-shaped structure in Khufu’s Pyramid by observation of cosmic-ray muons
sources.notes: Human-approved. Supports a separate North Face Corridor behind the Chevron, approximately 2.02 m wide, 2.18 m high, and 9.06 m long. Its original function is unknown and it must not be conflated with the Big Void.

sources.title: Les papyrus de la mer Rouge I. Le journal de Merer
sources.publication: Pierre Tallet, IFAO, MIFAO 136 (2017), ISBN 9782724707069; Papyrus B, sections BI–BIV, printed pp. 150–151
sources.notes: Human-approved. The published translation records Merer's team transporting fine limestone from Tura toward Akhet-Khufu. This is evidence of stone transport, not a complete account of pyramid engineering, all block movement, or the full workforce. Preserve fragmentary brackets and uncertainty.

sources.title: The Lost City of the Pyramids (Heit el-Ghurab)
sources.publication: Ancient Egypt Research Associates (AERA), excavation project record
sources.notes: Human-approved. Supports a 4th Dynasty settlement exceeding 7 hectares with workshops, industrial yards, bakeries, kitchens, warehouses, houses, and administrative spaces. AERA links it to the Giza pyramid complexes and says Khufu's link is probable, not certain.

sources.title: Some Notes on the Graffiti Written on the Cover Stones from the Second Boat Pit of Khufu
sources.publication: Takahashi and Nishisaka, Bulletin of the Society for Near Eastern Studies in Japan 59(1), 2–13 (2016), DOI 10.5356/jorient.59.1_2
sources.notes: Human-approved as a source for an attributed scholarly interpretation only. The authors propose that graffiti may reflect different stages or work groups in stone transport. Preserve uncertainty and attribution. Not used to support a canonical claim yet because the current ledger validator requires two distinct approved sources for a DEBATED claim.

sources.title: AERA Annual Report 2023–2024: The Great Pyramid Scanning Project
sources.publication: Ancient Egypt Research Associates, Annual Report 2023–2024 (published 2025), printed pp. 8–9
sources.notes: Human-approved. Supports ongoing documentation of bedrock features around Khufu's complex, including postholes, lever sockets, and quarry channels. The report describes an ongoing survey, not a complete or settled reconstruction of the construction method. Correct reference is printed pp. 8–9, not p. 7.

sources.title: The Great Pyramid
sources.publication: Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Discover Egypt's Monuments
sources.notes: Human-approved for contextual baseline only. The 10–20 year construction duration is an estimate, and the official page says the exact construction method is not entirely certain. Do not use this page as specialist proof of disputed engineering details.
